To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the laparoscopic treatment of endometriomas is as effective as the open technique in terms of pain relief and fertility; 2) laparoscopic excision of deep endometriosis lesions does not seem to reduce the chances for conception; 3) the use of laparoscopy for the treatment of colorectal endometrosis is associated with a higher rate of spontaneous conception compared with the open approach.

(1) endometriosis surgery is not a contraindication to future conception and should not lead to definitive infertility, (2) surgery for endometriomas can be performed with preservation of the ovarian reserve and with the same chances of spontaneous conception as ovarian cystectomy, (3) laparoscopy for colorectal endometryosis should be preferred to laparotomy, (4) surgery for deep endometriosis does not impair future conception by IVF, and
surgery for endometriosis should not be performed to the detriment of the procreative function and that surgery should be adapted to the patient’s desire for future conception.

endometrioma ablation and excision and their effect on fertility.
the surgical treatment of endometriotic disease and the preservation of fertility in women.
endometriotic surgery and preservation of future fertility.
